'''David Earl Nichols''' (born December 23, 1944) is an American [[pharmacologist]] and [[medicinal chemist]].<ref name="Oberhaus2017">{{cite web | last=Oberhaus | first=Daniel | title=America's Trippiest Chemist: Making Psychedelics 'Was Fun' | website=VICE | date=2 June 2017 | url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/psychedelic-drug-chemist-dave-nichols/ | access-date=18 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="url">{{cite web|url=http://www.heffter.org/review/chapter5.pdf|title=The Heffter Review of Psychedelic Research, Volume 1, 1998 - 5. The Medicinal Chemistry of Phenethylamine Psychedelics by David E. Nichols, Ph.D.|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080704190159/http://www.heffter.org/review/chapter5.pdf|archive-date=2008-07-04}}</ref>  
Previously the Robert C. and Charlotte P. Anderson Distinguished Chair in Pharmacology at [[Purdue University]], Nichols has worked in the field of [[psychoactive]] drugs since 1969.<ref name="Oberhaus2017" /> While still a graduate student, he patented the method that is used to make the optical [[isomers]] of [[psychedelic drug|psychedelic]] [[substituted amphetamine|amphetamine]]s. His contributions include the synthesis and reporting of [[escaline]], [[LSZ]], [[6-APB]], [[2C-I-NBOMe]] and other NBOMe variants ([[NBOMe-2C-B]], [[NBOMe-2C-C]], [[NBOMe-2C-D]]), and several others, as well as the coining of the term "[[entactogen]]".

He is the founding president of the [[Heffter Research Institute]], named after [[Germany|German]] chemist and pharmacologist [[Arthur Heffter]], who first discovered that [[mescaline]] was the active component in the [[peyote]] cactus. In 2004 he was named the Irwin H. Page Lecturer by the former International [[Serotonin]] Club (now the International Society for Serotonin Research),<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.serotoninclub.org/ |title=Home |website=serotoninclub.org}}</ref> and delivered an address in Portugal titled, "35 years studying psychedelics: what a long strange trip it's been". Among pharmacologists, he is considered to be one of the world's top experts on [[psychedelics]]. He has also been described as the "greatest living psychedelic chemist" or "greatest living psychedelic scientist" by [[Hamilton Morris]] and others in the 2020s.<ref name="MorrisNichols2021">{{cite podcast | url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/podcast-34-four-59224393 | title=PODCAST 34: A Four Hour Interview with Dr. David E Nichols | website=[[Hamilton Morris#Podcast|The Hamilton Morris Podcast]] | publisher=Patreon | host=[[Hamilton Morris]] | date=27 November 2021 | archive-url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYWITI4fGJw | archive-date = 24 November 2022}}</ref><ref name="McGloughlin2026">{{cite podcast | host = Evan McGloughlin | series = Giant's Shoulder | number = 108 | title = Meet The Greatest Living Psychedelic Scientist You've Never Heard Of | others = David E. Nichols (interviewee) | url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6umTgXsW1lQ | date = 2 April 2026 | access-date = 18 July 2026}}</ref> Nichols's other professional activities include teaching medicinal chemistry and molecular pharmacology at Purdue University in [[West Lafayette, IN]], and teaching medical students at the [[Indiana University School of Medicine]]. He officially retired in 2012 but has continued to work in the field.<ref name="Oberhaus2017" /> As of 2019, Nichols was an adjunct professor at the UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy, Chapel Hill, NC.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pharmacy.unc.edu/news/directory/denichol/|title=David Nichols|access-date=9 February 2019|archive-date=6 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906133324/https://pharmacy.unc.edu/directory/denichol/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Nichols, PhD, Robert C. and Charlotte P. == Research areas ==
Nichols is still carrying out academic research on the chemistry of psychedelics. He has published approximately 250 scientific reports and book chapters, all describing the relationship between the structure of a molecule and its biological effects (often referred to as a [[Structure-activity relationship]], or SAR).  He has done extensive work using the rat model assay of drug discrimination in characterizing hallucinogenic drugs.<ref>{{Cite book|title = The Neuroscience of Hallucinations|author1=Renaud Jardri |author2=Arnaud Cachia |author3=Pierre Thomas |author4=Delphine Pins |publisher = Springer|year = 2012|isbn = 9781461441205|pages = 262–263}}</ref>  Although his research mostly uses rats, a number of compounds included in Shulgin's [[PIHKAL]] were actually first synthesized in Nichols's lab.  His lab also first developed [<sup>125</sup>[[iodine|I]]]-(R)-[[2,5-Dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine|DOI]] as a [[radioligand]].  Nichols is one of the few people who has published legitimate research on the chemistry and [[pharmacology]] of [[LSD]] in the last 20 years, and first reported that several LSD analogues, including [[ETH-LAD]], [[PRO-LAD]], and [[AL-LAD]], were more potent than LSD itself.  Their human effects are described in [[TiHKAL]].  He also improved the synthesis of [[psilocybin]] so that it could be accessible for several recent clinical studies.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Nichols, David E |first1= Frescas, Stewart|date= 1999|title= Improvements to the synthesis of psilocybin and a facile method for preparing the O-acetyl prodrug of psilocin |url= https://www.doi.org/10.1055/s-1999-3490|journal= Synthesis|volume= 1999 |issue= 6 |pages= 935–938|doi= 10.1055/s-1999-3490 |access-date= October 18, 2024|url-access= subscription}}</ref>

Other notable research that he helped carry out includes extensive studies of the structure-activity relationships and mechanisms of action of [[3,4-Methylenedioxyamphetamine|MDA]] and [[MDMA]], during which he helped to discover many novel analogues including such compounds as [[3-Methyl-4,5-methylenedioxyamphetamine|5-methyl-MDA]], [[4-MTA]] and [[MDAI]]. Nichols has said that he believes gray-market chemists used information from papers he published on [[4-methylthioamphetamine]] (MTA) in the 1990s to synthesize the drug, which they sold in tablets nicknamed "flatliners" as a substitute for [[MDMA]] (Ecstasy).<ref>[[Jacob Sullum|Sullum, Jacob]] (2011-01-06) [http://reason.com/blog/2011/01/06/if-only-there-were-some-way-to If Only There Were Some Way to Discourage the Marketing of Dangerous Substitutes for Banned Drugs...], ''[[Reason Magazine|Reason]]''</ref>

More recently, Nichols has become one of the world leaders in research on [[dopamine]], and his team has developed several notable dopamine receptor [[ligand]]s, including the selective [[Dopamine receptor D1|D<sub>1</sub>]] full agonist compounds [[dihydrexidine]] and [[dinapsoline]] which have been researched for the treatment of [[Parkinson's disease]], as well as a number of other subtype-selective dopamine agonists derived from [[dinoxyline]]. He co-founded DarPharma, Inc. to commercialize his dopamine compounds; several of his team's compounds are now being studied in clinical trials for the treatment of Parkinson's disease and the cognitive and memory deficits of [[schizophrenia]].

== Impact on the designer drug market ==
[[Designer drug]] producers who scan scientific literature for information on compounds with potential [[grey market]] value have described Nichols' publications as an "especially valuable" road map to making new designer drugs.<ref>{{cite web|last=Whalen|first=Jeanne|title=In Quest for 'Legal High,' Chemists Outfox Law|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748704763904575550200845267526|date=Oct 30, 2010|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|access-date=10 September 2013}}</ref> Several deaths have been attributed to compounds that have been discovered in Nichols' lab, which he finds quite upsetting, "I was stunned by this revelation, and it left me with a hollow and depressed feeling for some time."<ref name="Nature">{{cite journal|last=Nichols|first=David|title=Legal highs: the dark side of medicinal chemistry|date=5 January 2011|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=469|issue=7|page=7|doi=10.1038/469007a|pmid=21209630|bibcode=2011Natur.469....7N|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Nichols has disclosed that he is writing three books as of the 2020s.<ref name="JikomesNichols2021">{{cite podcast | url=https://www.nickjikomes.com/audio-episodes/episode/48aee692/david-nichols-lsd-mescaline-mdma-dmt-and-psychedelics-as-medicine-or-33 | title=LSD, Mescaline, DMT, MDMA, Medicinal Chemistry & Psychedelic Medicine <nowiki>|</nowiki> David Nichols <nowiki>|</nowiki> 33 | website=Nick Jikomes | publisher=Mind & Matter Podcast: Science, Health, Metabolism | host=Nick Jikomes | date=19 August 2021 | quote = [50:44] So it's like I want to write some books. I haven't had a chance to write books but yeah I haven't I have not completely withdrawn from the field entirely. [50:54] What uh what do you want to write about? [50:57] Well I someone told me I should write my memoirs and I thought nobody's going to be interested and then my oldest son said yeah yeah people would be interested to hear about you so maybe I have um years of correspondence with Sasha Shogun. And I thought of a book called Conversations with Sasha where I pulled out little nuggets from our correspondents. And then I have a science fiction book that I'm I have the idea for that I'm working on. [...]}}</ref><ref name="McKennaNichols2024">{{cite podcast | url=https://mckenna.academy/mka-podcast/the-alchemist-reflections-on-a-lifetime-of-psychedelic-chemistry/ | title=The Alchemist: Reflections on a Lifetime of Psychedelic Chemistry | website=Brainforest Café Podcast | publisher=McKenna Academy of Natural Philosophy | host=[[Dennis McKenna]] | date=14 February 2024 | quote = [00:05:26] Dave Nichols: I’m writing my memoir and the title is The Accidental Professor. [00:05:32] Dennis McKenna: There you go. That’s a good one. So you’re writing a memoir? [00:05:38] Dave Nichols: Yeah. [00:05:44] Dennis McKenna: When is that going to be published? [00:05:47] Dave Nichols: Oh, I don’t know. I have to find somebody that wants to publish it first. I’m going through doing final edits. The beginning is boring. It’s about my early life. And then I get into sort of my sociopathic behavior as a teenager, making explosives and tear gas and blowing things up, and then got into graduate school and somehow managed to end up working on psychedelics. And from there on it was like in my groove. [...]}}</ref> These books include a [[memoir]], a collection of his letters with [[Alexander Shulgin]], and a [[science fiction]] [[novel]].<ref name="JikomesNichols2021" /><ref name="McKennaNichols2024" />
